title: MCMC without theatre
dek: Markov chain Monte Carlo draws from a posterior by simulating a Markov chain whose stationary law is p(θ | y). Diagnostics are part of the result; pretty traces are not a posterior.
story: When p(θ | y) has no closed form, you build a Markov chain θ^{(t)} such that, after a burn-in you must justify, the time average of g(θ^{(t)}) estimates E[g(θ) | y]. Metropolis–Hastings proposes a move and accepts with min(1, posterior ratio × proposal ratio). Gibbs updates full conditionals when they are conjugate. Hamiltonian Monte Carlo uses gradients to propose better moves in high dimension.
The chain is not the posterior. A histogram of draws is a Monte Carlo estimate of the posterior. If the chain has not mixed, the histogram is a portrait of where you started plus a local trap.

Report: several chains from dispersed starts, overlap (R̂ near 1 as a necessary not sufficient check), effective sample size for the functionals you quote, and divergences or rejected leaps if you used HMC. A single long chain with R̂ undefined is not a flex.
deepTitle: Accept/reject, ESS, and what can silently fail
deep: Metropolis–Hastings ratio for a target π(θ) = p(θ | y): accept with α = min(1, [π(θ') q(θ|θ')] / [π(θ) q(θ'|θ)]). When q is symmetric, the q terms cancel. You never need the marginal m(y); it cancels in π(θ')/π(θ). That is the whole trick.

Effective sample size: autocorrelated draws carry less information than iid posterior draws. ESS ≈ B / (1 + 2 ∑ ρ_t) in a crude AR picture. Quote Monte Carlo SEs, especially for tail quantiles of a rare-allele probability.

Funnel geometries (a hierarchical τ near 0 with many unit effects) break naive random-walk Metropolis and stress HMC. Reparameterise (non-centred) rather than “raise adapt_delta until the warning goes away” as a lifestyle.

A model that does not identify θ produces a chain that wanders along a ridge. That is a scientific message. Tightening a prior until the chain looks pretty is a different paper than the one you started.

formulas.label: Metropolis–Hastings accept
formulas.note: π(θ) ∝ f(y|θ) p(θ). The marginal likelihood cancels.

formulas.label: Ergodic average
formulas.note: Needs stationarity + ergodicity. Diagnostics argue for that, they do not prove it.

visual.caption: MCMC as a loop with an exit to diagnostics. Draws become a posterior estimate only after mixing and ESS are argued. The accept/reject node is Metropolis; HMC replaces the proposal, not the need for checks.

example.title: A two-parameter logit and a ridge
example.setup: Logit with two almost collinear covariates (lineage dummy and a SNP in perfect LD with lineage). Posterior of (β_lin, β_snp) is a ridge. A short Metropolis run looks “converged” in each margin and lies in 2-D.

steps.title: Look at the joint
steps.body: Scatter of draws: a diagonal cloud. Margins are wide. The chain may still mix along the ridge or it may stick. ESS for β_lin + β_snp (the identified sum) will be much higher than ESS for each coefficient.

steps.title: Scientific move
steps.body: Drop one covariate, or put a joint prior that encodes “these are two names for one effect,” or report the identified functional. More iterations will not invent a second piece of information.

steps.title: What to print
steps.body: R̂ and ESS for the functionals in the abstract, plus a sentence that the two coefficients are not separately identified. A pretty density of β_snp alone is theatre.

example.takeaway: MCMC estimates the posterior you wrote. If that posterior is a ridge, the honest output is a ridge.

check.prompt: Metropolis–Hastings can avoid computing the marginal likelihood m(y) because:
choices: m(y) cancels in the posterior ratio π(θ′)/π(θ)
You replace the likelihood by AIC
check.answer: m(y) cancels in the posterior ratio π(θ′)/π(θ)
check.why: π(θ) = f(y|θ)p(θ)/m(y). The ratio drops m(y). That is why MH is usable.

whyWrong.Priors cancel instead: Priors remain in the ratio unless they are equal.

check.prompt: You have 4000 post-warmup draws but ESS for a mean is 200. Relative to iid posterior draws, this is about:
choices: 20 times less information for that mean
check.answer: 20 times less information for that mean
check.why: 4000/200 = 20. Autocorrelation thinned the information. Tail quantiles are often worse.

whyWrong.the same information: ESS exists because it is not the same.

check.prompt: On the MCMC flow plate, why does “posterior summaries” sit behind a diagnostics node?
choices: Because traces are the scientific estimand
Because a histogram of unmixed draws is not yet a trustworthy estimate of p(θ|y)
Because ESS must equal n, the sample size of y
check.answer: Because a histogram of unmixed draws is not yet a trustworthy estimate of p(θ|y)
check.why: The plate’s whole point: computation, then argument for mixing, then numbers in the paper.

whyWrong.Because ESS must equal n, the sample siz: ESS is about MCMC draws, not n.
